thread:
priya: ap-east1 GPU allocs are failing right now, provisioning errors show `attach failed: IO error` on scratch NVMe nodes. Seeing a spike in provisioning latency and some checksum alerts. anyone digging in? :eyes:

ops-bot: ALERT: nvme_smart_threshold_exceeded on gnode-ae-42 (reallocations rising) — severity: warning

alex: looking. quick `iostat -x 1 3` from a impacted node:```
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.00  12.00  0.25 98.50  1.00 512.00   10.36   9.87  35.2  0.8    35.4   1.20  99.95
```
This looks like full saturation (almost 100% util) and avg queue ~10.

martin: confirmed — janitor/ephemeral-cleaner has been running a big pass (concurrency=24) after yesterday's backlog. It's doing a lot of small unlink ops which kill IOPS.

marta: do we know if it's the deletes causing checksum spikes or we're seeing underlying flash degradation?

alex: two things: 1) small random deletes blow up IO; 2) a couple of nodes (gnode-ae-42, gnode-ae-47) show SMART reallocated sector count tick up. Could be both.

priya: immediate mitigation plan: (A) throttle janitor to reduce concurrency, (B) divert new GPU allocations to us-west2 dedicated pool for the next 2h, (C) cordon/quarantine the top degrading nodes. Thoughts?

martin: agree. throttle first. reducing concurrency to 4 should drop IOPS significantly. But backlog will grow — we'll need a controlled, rate-limited cleaner rather than an all-at-once sweep.

alex: command to apply now:```bash
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/ephemeral-cleaner CLEANER_CONCURRENCY=4
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/ephemeral-cleaner
```
I'm running it now.

ops-bot: deploy triggered: rollout/ephemeral-cleaner restarted by alex — rollout started.

marta: routing GPUs to us-west2 increases egress/cross-region latency and cost. How long do we keep it?

priya: estimate 2 hours for immediate stabilization, then monitor. If janitor rate-limiter patch lands quickly we can open allocations sooner. Cost tradeoff is acceptable vs app-level outages.

alex: cordoning the worst node:```bash
kubectl cordon gnode-ae-42 && kubectl drain gnode-ae-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
SMART dump shows:```
SMART overall-health: PASSED
Reallocated_Sector_Ct: 120 -> increased by 8 in last 24h
Uncorrectable_Error_Cnt: 3
```
Recommend quarantining until replacement.

martin: I'll open a hardware ticket and tag hwops. Also adding an ephemeral scrub schedule change to avoid back-to-back sweeps at midnight.

priya: can we temporarily change the cleaner strategy to batch-delete per directory (larger sequential IO) instead of millions of tiny unlink syscalls? That would help.

alex: quick patch is to make cleaner use buffered rm script that groups deletes per prefix for 30s windows. I'll open a quick PR as a hotfix and a proper design RFC later.

deploy-bot: PR #4821 opened by alex: "ephemeral-cleaner: group deletes into buckets and add rate limiter" — CI passed, requesting review.

marta: fine, but ensure we don't keep too big of a backlog. Need visibility on backlog size. Can we add a metric `ephemeral.cleaner.backlog_bytes`?

martin: adding metric now. Also enabling a per-node concurrency cap based on nvme %util in prometheus alerting.

ops-bot: MONITORING: alert rule created `NVME_IO_THROTTLE_HIGH` (expr: avg_over_time(node_disk_util[2m]) > 0.85) — notify eng-infra paging.

priya: alex — once the PR merges, do a canary in ap-east1 small subset (10 nodes) then we can slowly reopen allocations. Also we should schedule node replacements for any with reallocated > 100.

alex: PR merged and rolled out canary to gnode-ae-{50..59}. Observed avg queue drop from ~9 to ~2 within 5m. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout complete — 10 nodes healthy.

marta: good progress. For the RFC, include cost delta for routing to other regions and a proposal for adaptive cleaning (backoff, group deletes, cap by node util).

priya: routing lifted for low-priority jobs at 1739504000, keep high-priority GPU allocs still hitting fallback until further notice. Monitoring dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/ephemeral-cleaner

martin: created TICKET-8742 to replace two drives and follow-up RFC (link: https://tickets.internal/TICKET-8742).

priya: summary: throttled cleaner, quarantined two nodes, canary hotfix for grouping deletes deployed, routing fallback used for 2h window, follow-up RFC + hw ticket created. Close the loop after 24h metrics check. Thanks all. :heart:
